units.zh: 季布者，楚人也。
units.en: Ji Bu was a native of Chu.
units.literal: Ji Bu was a man of Chu.

units.zh: 為氣任俠，有名於楚。
units.en: A man of fierce spirit who lived as a knight-errant, he was famed throughout Chu.
units.literal: He was spirited and acted as a knight-errant, gaining great renown in Chu.

units.zh: 項籍使將兵，數窘漢王。
units.en: Xiang Ji appointed him to command troops, and on multiple occasions he drove the King of Han into desperate straits.
units.literal: Xiang Ji sent him to command troops, and he repeatedly put the Han King in dire straits.

units.zh: 及項羽滅，高祖購求布千金，敢有舍匿，罪及三族。
units.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Emperor Gaozu posted a bounty of a thousand gold pieces for Ji Bu's capture, decreeing that anyone who dared shelter or conceal him would have the punishment extended to three generations of their clan.
units.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Gaozu offered a thousand pieces of gold for Ji Bu's capture; anyone who dared harbor or conceal him would have the crime extend to three generations of his clan.

units.zh: 季布匿濮陽周氏。
units.en: Ji Bu went into hiding with the Zhou family in Puyang.
units.literal: Ji Bu hid with the Zhou family in Puyang.

units.zh: 周氏曰：「漢購將軍急，跡且至臣家，將軍能聽臣，臣敢獻計；
units.en: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for you, General, is urgent, and your trail will soon reach my house. If you, General, will heed me, I dare offer a plan;
units.literal: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for the general is urgent, and traces will soon reach my household. If the general can heed me, I dare offer a plan;

units.zh: 即不能，願先自剄。」
units.en: if not, I will slit my own throat first."
units.literal: if you cannot, I wish first to slit my own throat."

units.zh: 季布許之。
units.en: Ji Bu consented.
units.literal: Ji Bu agreed to this.

units.zh: 乃髡鉗季布，衣褐衣，置廣柳車中，并與其家僮數十人，之魯朱家所賣之。
units.en: They shaved Ji Bu's head, clamped an iron collar around his neck, dressed him in coarse cloth, and placed him in a broad-sided cart. Together with dozens of household slaves, they transported him to the estate of Zhu Jia in Lu and sold him there.
units.literal: They shaved Ji Bu's head, fitted him with an iron collar, dressed him in coarse hemp clothing, placed him in a wide willow cart, and along with several dozen of his household slaves, took him to be sold to Zhu Jia of Lu.

units.zh: 朱家心知是季布，乃買而置之田。
units.en: Zhu Jia secretly recognized that this was Ji Bu. He purchased him and set him to work in the fields.
units.literal: Zhu Jia recognized in his heart that this was Ji Bu, so he bought him and put him to work in the fields.

units.zh: 誡其子曰：「田事聽此奴，必與同食。」
units.en: He admonished his son, saying, "In the fields, take orders from this slave; you must eat at the same table with him."
units.literal: He admonished his son, saying, "In field affairs obey this slave; you must eat with him."

units.zh: 朱家乃乘軺車之洛陽，見汝陰侯滕公。
units.en: Zhu Jia then rode a light carriage to Luoyang, where he called upon Xiahou Ying, the Marquis of Ruyin.
units.literal: Zhu Jia then rode in a light carriage to Luoyang and saw the Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong.

units.zh: 滕公留朱家飲數日。
units.en: The Marquis kept Zhu Jia as his guest and drank with him for several days.
units.literal: Teng Gong detained Zhu Jia and feasted him for several days.

units.zh: 因謂滕公曰：「季布何大罪，而上求之急也？」
units.en: He then asked Teng Gong, "What grave offense has Ji Bu committed, for the Sovereign to pursue him with such urgency?"
units.literal: Then he said to Teng Gong, "What great crime has Ji Bu committed, that the Sovereign seeks him so urgently?"

units.zh: 滕公曰：「布數為項羽窘上，上怨之，故必欲得之。」
units.en: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to capture him."
units.literal: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to have him."

units.zh: 朱家曰：「君視季布何如人也？」
units.en: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'
units.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'

units.zh: 曰：「賢者也。」
units.en: Teng Gong said, "A worthy man."
units.literal: He said, "A worthy man."

units.zh: 朱家曰：「臣各為其主用，季布為項籍用，職耳。
units.en: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.
units.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.

units.zh: 項氏臣可盡誅邪？
units.en: Should all Xiang Yu's ministers be executed?
units.literal: Xiang clan ministers can all execute?

units.zh: 今上始得天下，獨以己之私怨求一人，何示天下之不廣也！
units.en: Now that the Sovereign has just won the empire, to hunt one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of narrow-mindedness to all under heaven!
units.literal: Now that the Sovereign has just obtained the empire, to seek one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of lack of magnanimity to all under heaven!

units.zh: 且以季布之賢而漢求之急如此，此不北走胡即南走越耳。
units.en: Moreover, with a man as worthy as Ji Bu sought by Han with such urgency, he will either flee north to the Xiongnu or south to the Yue.
units.literal: Moreover, with Ji Bu's worthiness and Han seek him urgent like this, this not north flee Hu then south flee Yue only.

units.zh: 夫忌壯士以資敵國，此伍子胥所以鞭荊平王之墓也。
units.en: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby strengthen enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.
units.literal: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby aid enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.

units.zh: 君何不從容為上言邪？」
units.en: Why not find a calm moment to speak to the Sovereign about this?"
units.literal: Why do you not speak to the Sovereign about this at your leisure?"

units.zh: 汝陰侯滕公心知朱家大俠，意季布匿其所，乃許曰：「諾。」
units.en: The Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong, knew in his heart that Zhu Jia was a great knight-errant, and suspected that Ji Bu was hiding in his home. He then agreed, saying, 'Very well.'
units.literal: Ruyin Hou Teng Gong heart knew Zhu Jia great knight-errant, suspected Ji Bu concealed his place, then promised said: 'Yes.'

units.zh: 待閒，果言如朱家指。
units.en: When he had a suitable moment, he spoke to the Emperor exactly as Zhu Jia had urged.
units.literal: He waited for a leisurely moment, and indeed spoke as Zhu Jia had directed.

units.zh: 上乃赦季布。
units.en: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Ji Bu.
units.literal: The Sovereign then pardoned Ji Bu.

units.zh: 當是時，諸公皆多季布能摧剛為柔，朱家亦以此名聞當世。
units.en: At that time, everyone praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia likewise won renown throughout the age for this.
units.literal: At this time, all the nobles praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia also gained fame in the present age through this.

units.zh: 季布召見，謝，上拜為郎中。
units.en: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed his gratitude. The Emperor appointed him as a Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed thanks. The Sovereign appointed him as a lang zhong (court attendant).

units.zh: 孝惠時，為中郎將。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Hui, he served as Commander of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: During Emperor Hui's reign, he served as zhong lang jiang (lieutenant general).

units.zh: 單于嘗為書嫚呂后，不遜，呂后大怒，召諸將議之。
units.en: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms. Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned all the generals to discuss it.
units.literal: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms; Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned the generals to discuss it.

units.zh: 上將軍樊噲曰：「臣願得十萬眾，橫行匈奴中。」
units.en: The Supreme General, Fan Kuai, said, 'I wish to obtain a force of 100,000 men and march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands.'
units.literal: Supreme General Fan Kuai said, "Your servant wishes to have a force of one hundred thousand and rampage through the Xiongnu lands."

units.zh: 諸將皆阿呂后意，曰「然」。
units.en: All the generals flattered Empress Lü's wishes and said, 'Yes.'
units.literal: Various generals all flattered Empress Lü's intention, said 'Yes'.

units.zh: 季布曰：「樊噲可斬也！
units.en: Ji Bu said, 'Fan Kuai should be executed!
units.literal: Ji Bu said: 'Fan Kuai can behead!

units.zh: 夫高帝將兵四十餘萬眾，困於平城，今噲柰何以十萬眾橫行匈奴中，面欺！
units.en: Indeed, when the Gao Emperor led over 400,000 troops, he was trapped at Pingcheng. Now how can Kuai march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands with 100,000 men? This is barefaced deception!
units.literal: Indeed Gao Emperor led troops forty more myriad multitude, trapped at Pingcheng, now Kuai how with ten myriad multitude rampage Xiongnu midst, face deceive!

units.zh: 且秦以事於胡，陳勝等起。
units.en: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose in revolt.
units.literal: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose up.

units.zh: 于今創痍未瘳，噲又面諛，欲搖動天下。」
units.en: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Fan Kuai again flatters you to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'
units.literal: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Kuai again flatters to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'

units.zh: 是時殿上皆恐，太后罷朝，遂不復議擊匈奴事。
units.en: At this, everyone in the hall fell silent with fear. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and the matter of attacking the Xiongnu was never raised again.
units.literal: At this time, all in the hall were terrified. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and they never again discussed attacking the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 季布為河東守，孝文時，人有言其賢者，孝文召，欲以為御史大夫。
units.en: Ji Bu was serving as the Governor of Hedong when, during the reign of Emperor Wen, certain people praised his worthiness. Emperor Wen summoned him, intending to appoint him as the Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Ji Bu served as governor of Hedong. During Emperor Wen's reign, people spoke of his worthiness, so Emperor Wen summoned him, intending to appoint him as Yushi Dafu (Censor-in-Chief).

units.zh: 復有言其勇，使酒難近。
units.en: But then others reported that although he was brave, he became belligerent when drunk and was difficult to deal with.
units.literal: Others again spoke of his bravery, but said that when he drank wine he was difficult to approach.

units.zh: 至，留邸一月，見罷。
units.en: Ji Bu arrived and was kept waiting at the state guesthouse for a month before being granted an audience and then dismissed.
units.literal: He arrived and was detained at the guesthouse for a month, then given an audience and dismissed.

units.zh: 季布因進曰：「臣無功竊寵，待罪河東。
units.en: Ji Bu then stepped forward and said, "Your servant has no merit yet has stealthily received favor, and stands awaiting punishment in Hedong.
units.literal: Ji Bu then advanced and said, "Your servant has no merit yet has stealthily received favor, and stands awaiting punishment in Hedong.

units.zh: 陛下無故召臣，此人必有以臣欺陛下者；
units.en: Your Majesty summoned me without cause—someone must have deceived Your Majesty about me;
units.literal: Your Majesty without cause summoned minister, this person must have with minister deceived Your Majesty;

units.zh: 今臣至，無所受事，罷去，此人必有以毀臣者。
units.en: Now I have arrived, received no duties, and been sent away—someone must have slandered me to Your Majesty.
units.literal: Now I have arrived and received no assignments, then been dismissed—this person must have slandered me.

units.zh: 夫陛下以一人之譽而召臣，一人之毀而去臣，臣恐天下有識聞之有以闚陛下也。」
units.en: If Your Majesty summons me because one man praises me and sends me away because one man slanders me, I fear that perceptive men throughout the empire, once they hear of it, will have reason to look into Your Majesty's judgment."
units.literal: For Your Majesty to summon me on one man's praise and send me away on one man's slander—I fear that the knowledgeable throughout the empire who hear of it will have grounds to scrutinize Your Majesty."

units.zh: 上默然慚，良久曰：「河東吾股肱郡，故特召君耳。」
units.en: The Emperor fell silent, ashamed; after a long while he said, "Hedong is my vital commandery, so I specially summoned you."
units.literal: The Sovereign fell silent, ashamed; after a long while he said, "Hedong is my arm-and-thigh commandery, so I specially summoned you."

units.zh: 布辭之官。
units.en: Ji Bu took his leave and returned to his post.
units.literal: Ji Bu took his leave and returned to his office.

units.zh: 楚人曹丘生，辯士，數招權顧金錢。
units.en: There was a man of Chu named Cao Qiu Sheng, a persuasive rhetorician who repeatedly sought influence and pursued gold and money.
units.literal: Cao Qiu Sheng of Chu was a persuasive rhetorician who repeatedly sought influence and pursued gold and money.

units.zh: 事貴人趙同等，與竇長君善。
units.en: He had attached himself to prominent figures such as Zhao Tong and was on friendly terms with Dou Changjun.
units.literal: He served noble persons like Zhao Tong and was on good terms with Dou Changjun.

units.zh: 季布聞之，寄書諫竇長君曰：「吾聞曹丘生非長者，勿與通。」
units.en: Ji Bu heard this and sent a letter admonishing Dou Changjun, saying, 'I have heard that Cao Qiu Sheng is not an upright person—do not associate with him.'
units.literal: Ji Bu heard this, sent letter admonished Dou Changjun said: 'I heard Cao Qiu Sheng not upright person, do not with communicate.'

units.zh: 及曹丘生歸，欲得書請季布。
units.en: When Cao Qiu returned home, he wished to obtain a letter of introduction to Ji Bu.
units.literal: When Cao Qiu Sheng returned, he wished to obtain a letter to request an introduction to Ji Bu.

units.zh: 竇長君曰：「季將軍不說足下，足下無往。」
units.en: Dou Changjun said, 'General Ji is not pleased with you—you should not go.'
units.literal: Dou Changjun said: 'Ji general not pleased you, you no go.'

units.zh: 固請書，遂行。
units.en: But he insisted on having the letter and set off regardless.
units.literal: He firmly requested the letter and then went.

units.zh: 使人先發書，季布果大怒，待曹丘。
units.en: He sent a messenger ahead with the letter. Ji Bu, as expected, flew into a rage and waited for Cao Qiu's arrival, ready to confront him.
units.literal: He sent someone to deliver the letter first, and Ji Bu indeed became greatly angered, waiting for Cao Qiu.

units.zh: 曹丘至，即揖季布曰：「楚人諺曰『得黃金百（斤），不如得季布一諾』，足下何以得此聲於梁楚閒哉？
units.en: Cao Qiu arrived and immediately bowed to Ji Bu, saying, 'The Chu people have a proverb: "Getting a hundred jin of yellow gold is not as good as getting one promise from Ji Bu." How did you, sir, obtain this reputation between Liang and Chu?
units.literal: Cao Qiu arrived, immediately bowed Ji Bu said: 'Chu people proverb says 'obtain yellow gold hundred (jin), not as obtain Ji Bu one promise', you sir how obtained this reputation in Liang Chu between?

units.zh: 且仆楚人，足下亦楚人也。
units.en: Besides, I am a man of Chu, and you too are a man of Chu.
units.literal: Moreover, I am a Chu person, and you, sir, are also a Chu person.

units.zh: 仆游揚足下之名於天下，顧不重邪？
units.en: I have traveled and spread your reputation throughout the empire—is this not a weighty matter?
units.literal: I travel spread you sir's name in tianxia, but not heavy?

units.zh: 何足下距仆之深也！」
units.en: Why do you, sir, reject me so deeply!'
units.literal: Why you sir reject I so deep!'

units.zh: 季布乃大說，引入，留數月，為上客，厚送之。
units.en: Ji Bu was greatly pleased. He invited Cao Qiu in, kept him as a guest for several months, treated him with the highest honor, and sent him off with lavish gifts.
units.literal: Ji Bu was then greatly pleased, led him in, detained him for several months, treated him as an honored guest, and richly sent him off.

units.zh: 季布名所以益聞者，曹丘揚之也。
units.en: The reason Ji Bu's reputation grew ever greater was that Cao Qiu had spread it far and wide.
units.literal: The reason Ji Bu's reputation became increasingly well-known was that Cao Qiu spread it.

units.zh: 季布弟季心，氣蓋關中，遇人恭謹，為任俠，方數千里，士皆爭為之死。
units.en: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin possessed a spirit that overawed all Guanzhong. He treated others with respectful courtesy and lived as a knight-errant; across a region of several thousand li, gentlemen all competed for the chance to die on his behalf.
units.literal: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin had a spirit that overshadowed all of Guanzhong. He treated people with respectful courtesy and lived as a knight-errant; within a region of several thousand li, gentlemen were all eager to die for him.

units.zh: 嘗殺人，亡之吳，從袁絲匿。
units.en: He once killed a man, fled to Wu, and took refuge with Yuan Si.
units.literal: He once killed a person, fled to Wu, and hid with Yuan Si.

units.zh: 長事袁絲，弟畜灌夫、籍福之屬。
units.en: For many years he served Yuan Si as an elder, while treating men such as Guan Fu and Ji Fu as younger brothers under his protection.
units.literal: He long served Yuan Si as to an elder, and treated men like Guan Fu and Ji Fu as younger brothers under his care.

units.zh: 嘗為中司馬，中尉郅都不敢不加禮。
units.en: He once served as a Palace Marshal, and even Zhi Du, the Commandant of Justice, did not dare treat him with anything less than full courtesy.
units.literal: He once served as zhong sima, and even the zhong wei Zhi Du dared not fail to show him proper respect.

units.zh: 少年多時時竊籍其名以行。
units.en: Young men of the day often invoked his name without permission to further their own ends.
units.literal: Young men often secretly borrowed his name from time to time to carry out their affairs.

units.zh: 當是時，季心以勇，布以諾，著聞關中。
units.en: In those days, Ji Xin was celebrated for his courage and Ji Bu for the reliability of his word—both were famous throughout Guanzhong.
units.literal: At this time, Ji Xin was known for bravery and Ji Bu for keeping his word—their reputations were prominent throughout Guanzhong.

units.zh: 季布母弟丁公，為楚將。
units.en: Ji Bu's mother's younger brother Ding Gong served as a Chu general.
units.literal: Ji Bu mother's younger brother Ding Gong, served as Chu general.

units.zh: 丁公為項羽逐窘高祖彭城西，短兵接，高祖急，顧丁公曰：「兩賢豈相戹哉！」
units.en: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Emperor Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; the Emperor was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"
units.literal: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; Gaozu was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"

units.zh: 於是丁公引兵而還，漢王遂解去。
units.en: At this, Ding Gong withdrew his troops, and the King of Han was able to escape.
units.literal: So Ding Gong led his troops back, and the Han King thus escaped.

units.zh: 及項王滅，丁公謁見高祖。
units.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Ding Gong sought an audience with Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Ding Gong went for an audience with Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖以丁公徇軍中，曰：「丁公為項王臣不忠，使項王失天下者，乃丁公也。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served King Xiang as a minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."
units.literal: Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served as King Xiang's minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."

units.zh: 遂斬丁公，曰：「使後世為人臣者無效丁公！」
units.en: Gaozu then had Ding Gong beheaded, saying, "Let no minister in later generations follow Ding Gong's example!"
units.literal: He then beheaded Ding Gong, saying, "Let no minister in future generations imitate Ding Gong!"

units.zh: 欒布者，梁人也。
units.en: Luan Bu was a native of Liang.
units.literal: Luan Bu was a man of Liang.

units.zh: 始梁王彭越為家人時，嘗與布游。
units.en: In the early days, when Peng Yue—who would later become King of Liang—was still a commoner, he and Luan Bu had been companions.
units.literal: When the Liang King Peng Yue was still a commoner, he once roamed with Bu.

units.zh: 窮困，賃傭於齊，為酒人保。
units.en: Destitute, Luan Bu hired himself out as a laborer in Qi and worked as a guard at a tavern.
units.literal: He was impoverished and distressed, hired himself out as labor in Qi, and served as security at a tavern.

units.zh: 數歲，彭越去之巨野中為盜，而布為人所略賣，為奴於燕。
units.en: After several years, Peng Yue departed for the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Luan Bu was kidnapped and sold into slavery in Yan.
units.literal: After several years, Peng Yue went into the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Bu was abducted and sold by people, becoming a slave in Yan.

units.zh: 為其家主報仇，燕將臧荼舉以為都尉。
units.en: He avenged his master's death, and the Yan general Zang Tu, impressed, recommended him to the rank of District Commandant.
units.literal: He avenged his household master, and the Yan general Zang Tu recommended him to serve as du wei.

units.zh: 臧荼後為燕王，以布為將。
units.en: When Zang Tu later became King of Yan, he appointed Luan Bu as one of his generals.
units.literal: Zang Tu later became King of Yan and appointed Bu as his general.

units.zh: 及臧荼反，漢擊燕，虜布。
units.en: When Zang Tu rebelled, the Han forces attacked Yan and took Luan Bu prisoner.
units.literal: When Zang Tu rebelled, Han attacked Yan and captured Bu.

units.zh: 梁王彭越聞之，乃言上，請贖布以為梁大夫。
units.en: When the King of Liang, Peng Yue, heard of this, he petitioned the Emperor to ransom Luan Bu and appoint him as a Minister of Liang.
units.literal: The Liang King Peng Yue heard this and then spoke to the Sovereign, requesting to redeem Bu to serve as a Liang daifu (minister).

units.zh: 使於齊，未還，漢召彭越，責以謀反，夷三族。
units.en: Luan Bu was sent on a diplomatic mission to Qi and had not yet returned when the Han court summoned Peng Yue, charged him with plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.
units.literal: He was sent on a mission to Qi and had not yet returned when Han summoned Peng Yue, blamed him for plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.

units.zh: 已而梟彭越頭於雒陽下，詔曰：「有敢收視者，輒捕之。」
units.en: Soon after, Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."
units.literal: Soon Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."

units.zh: 布從齊還，奏事彭越頭下，祠而哭之。
units.en: When Luan Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's severed head, made offerings, and wept for him.
units.literal: When Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's head, made offerings, and wept for him.

units.zh: 吏捕布以聞。
units.en: The officials arrested Luan Bu and reported the matter to the throne.
units.literal: The officials captured Bu and reported it.

units.zh: 上召布，罵曰：「若與彭越反邪？
units.en: The Emperor summoned Luan Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?
units.literal: The Sovereign summoned Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?

units.zh: 吾禁人勿收，若獨祠而哭之，與越反明矣。
units.en: I forbade anyone to attend to his remains, yet you alone made offerings and wept for him—it is clear you were part of Yue's rebellion.
units.literal: I prohibited people from collecting it, but you alone sacrificed and wept for him—it's clear you rebelled with Yue.

units.zh: 趣亨之。」
units.en: Hurry and execute him.'
units.literal: Hurry execute him.'

units.zh: 方提趣湯，布顧曰：「願一言而死。」
units.en: Just as they were leading him to hurry to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, 'I wish to speak one word before I die.'
units.literal: Just as they were leading him in haste to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, "I wish to speak one word before I die."

units.zh: 上曰：「何言？」
units.en: The Sovereign said, 'What words?'
units.literal: Sovereign said: 'What words?'

units.zh: 布曰：「方上之困於彭城，敗滎陽、成皋閒，項王所以（遂）不能［遂］西，徒以彭王居梁地，與漢合從苦楚也。
units.en: Bu said, 'When the Sovereign was distressed at Pengcheng and defeated between Xingyang and Chenggao, the reason Xiang Yu could not advance west was only because the Peng King dwelt in Liang lands and allied with Han to afflict Chu.
units.literal: Bu said: 'Just Sovereign's distress at Pengcheng, defeated between Xingyang, Chenggao, Xiang Wang reason not able west, only because Peng King dwelt Liang lands, with Han allied together afflicted Chu.

units.zh: 當是之時，彭王一顧，與楚則漢破，與漢而楚破。
units.en: At that moment, the fate of the empire hung on a single decision by the King of Peng: had he sided with Chu, Han would have been destroyed; because he sided with Han, Chu was destroyed.
units.literal: At this time, with just one glance from the Peng King, if he allied with Chu then Han would be broken, if he allied with Han then Chu would be broken.

units.zh: 且垓下之會，微彭王，項氏不亡。
units.en: Moreover, at the battle of Gaixia, without the King of Peng, the house of Xiang would never have fallen.
units.literal: Moreover, at the Gaixia meeting, without the Peng King, the Xiang clan would not have perished.

units.zh: 天下已定，彭王剖符受封，亦欲傳之萬世。
units.en: After the empire was settled, the King of Peng received his tally and his fief, and naturally wished to pass them down for ten thousand generations.
units.literal: The empire was already settled, the Peng King had his tally divided and received his fief, and he also wished to transmit it to ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 今陛下一徵兵於梁，彭王病不行，而陛下疑以為反，反形未見，以苛小案誅滅之，臣恐功臣人人自危也。
units.en: Now Your Majesty levied troops from Liang just once, and when the King of Peng was too ill to comply, Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. No evidence of rebellion was ever found, yet he was destroyed on a trivial pretext. I fear that every minister who has rendered meritorious service now feels his own life is in danger.
units.literal: Now Your Majesty summoned troops just once from Liang, the Peng King was ill and did not go, yet Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. The shape of rebellion was not seen, but you exterminated him with a harsh and petty case. I fear all the merit ministers will each feel endangered.

units.zh: 今彭王已死，臣生不如死，請就亨。」
units.en: Now that the Peng King is already dead, living is not as good as dying for me. Please proceed with the boiling.'
units.literal: Now Peng King already dead, minister living not as dying, please proceed boil.'

units.zh: 於是上乃釋布罪，拜為都尉。
units.en: Thereupon the Emperor released Luan Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.
units.literal: Thereupon the Sovereign released Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.

units.zh: 孝文時，為燕相，至將軍。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Wen, he served as the Chancellor of Yan and eventually rose to the rank of general.
units.literal: During Emperor Wen's reign, he served as prime minister of Yan and rose to the rank of general.

units.zh: 布乃稱曰：「窮困不能辱身下志，非人也；
units.en: Bu then declared, 'If poverty and distress cannot humiliate one's self or lower one's ambitions, that is not human;
units.literal: Bu then declared: 'Impoverished distressed cannot humiliate self lower ambitions, not person;

units.zh: 富貴不能快意，非賢也。」
units.en: If wealth and nobility cannot delight one's intentions, that is not worthy.'
units.literal: Wealth nobility cannot delight intentions, not worthy.'

units.zh: 於是嘗有德者厚報之，有怨者必以法滅之。
units.en: From then on, he repaid generously all those who had once shown him kindness, and those who had wronged him he invariably destroyed through the law.
units.literal: So he thickly repaid those who had once shown him virtue, and those who had grievances against him he certainly extinguished with the law.

units.zh: 吳（軍）［楚］反時，以軍功封俞侯，復為燕相。
units.en: During the time of the Wu [Chu] rebellion, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yu for military merit, and again served as prime minister of Yan.
units.literal: Wu (army) [Chu] rebellion time, with military merit enfeoffed Yu Hou, again served as Yan prime minister.

units.zh: 燕齊之閒皆為欒布立社，號曰欒公社。
units.en: Throughout the lands between Yan and Qi, the people established shrines in his honor, calling them the Shrines of Lord Luan.
units.literal: Between Yan and Qi, all established shrines for Luan Bu, calling them the Luan Gong shrines.

units.zh: 景帝中五年薨。
units.en: He died in the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing, he died.

units.zh: 子賁嗣，為太常，犧牲不如令，國除。
units.en: His son Ben inherited the title and served as the Grand Master of Ceremonies, but because the sacrificial animals he provided did not meet the prescribed standards, his fief was abolished.
units.literal: His son Ben succeeded him and served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, but his sacrifices did not conform to regulations, so his fief was eliminated.

units.zh: 太史公曰：以項羽之氣，而季布以勇顯於楚，身屨（典）軍搴旗者數矣，可謂壯士。
units.en: The Grand Historian said: In the age of Xiang Yu's fierce power, Ji Bu became renowned in Chu for his bravery; he personally commanded troops and seized enemy banners several times. He can indeed be called a stalwart warrior.
units.literal: The Grand Historian said: Under Xiang Yu's authority, Ji Bu nonetheless became famed in Chu for bravery; he personally led troops and seized enemy banners on several occasions—he may be called a stalwart warrior.

units.zh: 然至被刑戮，為人奴而不死，何其下也！
units.en: Yet when he reached the point of punishment and branding, became another man's slave, and still did not die, how low he sank!
units.literal: Yet when it came to suffering punishment and branding, becoming another man's slave and not dying—how base!

units.zh: 彼必自負其材，故受辱而不羞，欲有所用其未足也，故終為漢名將。
units.en: He must have been confident in his own abilities, and therefore accepted humiliation without shame, knowing that his talents had not yet been fully employed. In the end, he became one of the celebrated generals of Han.
units.literal: He certainly relied upon his own talents, therefore accepted humiliation without feeling shame, wishing to have some use for what was still insufficient, and therefore finally became a famous general of Han.

units.zh: 賢者誠重其死。
units.en: A truly worthy man weighs his death carefully.
units.literal: Truly, the worthy value their death.

units.zh: 夫婢妾賤人感慨而自殺者，非能勇也，其計畫無復之耳。
units.en: When slave girls, concubines, and people of low station kill themselves in a moment of passion, it is not because they are brave—it is because they see no way forward.
units.literal: Indeed, when concubines and base people are emotionally moved and commit suicide, it is not that they are able to be brave—their plans simply have no recovery.

units.zh: 欒布哭彭越，趣湯如歸者，彼誠知所處，不自重其死。
units.en: When Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and walked toward the boiling cauldron as calmly as if he were going home, it was because he truly understood his situation and did not cling to his own life.
units.literal: Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and hurried to the cauldron as if returning home—he truly knew his situation and did not value his own death.

units.zh: 雖往古烈士，何以加哉！
units.en: Even among the fierce warriors of antiquity, who could surpass this?
units.literal: Even the martyred warriors of old—how could one surpass this!
